gloss: feeling of impatience; sense of restless frustration

definitions.gloss: feeling of impatience; sense of restless frustration; anxiety-driven restlessness
definitions.explanation: An uneasy, agitated feeling of being unable to wait or stay still, often arising from frustration at things not going as planned or from a sense of urgency.

examples.japanese: {焦燥感|しょうそうかん}に{駆|か}られる。
examples.english: To be driven by a sense of impatience.

examples.japanese: {締|し}め{切|き}りが{近|ちか}づくにつれて{焦燥感|しょうそうかん}が{増|ま}してきた。
examples.english: My sense of restless frustration grew as the deadline approached.

examples.japanese: {結果|けっか}が{出|で}ないまま{時間|じかん}だけが{過|す}ぎていく{焦燥感|しょうそうかん}は、{誰|だれ}にでも{経験|けいけん}があるだろう。
examples.english: Everyone has probably experienced the frustration of time passing without results.

notes: Common collocations: {焦燥感|しょうそうかん}に{駆|か}られる (to be seized by restless frustration), {焦燥感|しょうそうかん}を{覚|おぼ}える (to feel a sense of impatience), {焦燥感|しょうそうかん}が{募|つの}る (for restless frustration to build up). The suffix ～{感|かん} (feeling, sense) creates emotion nouns: {不安感|ふあんかん} (sense of unease), {達成感|たっせいかん} (sense of achievement), {疎外感|そがいかん} (sense of alienation). The base word {焦燥|しょうそう} (impatience, irritation) is less common on its own. Related: {苛立|いらだ}ち (irritation — more everyday), {焦|あせ}り (impatience — more colloquial).
